edges.description: WNT4 is required for the formation and elongation of the Mullerian duct, so loss of WNT4 signalling prevents the duct and its derivatives from forming.
WNT4 normally represses steroidogenic enzyme expression in the ovary; the mutant proteins fail to do so.

Wnt4 is required in the metanephric mesenchyme for the mesenchyme-to-epithelium conversion that forms nephrons. This edge rests on homozygous null mouse data; whether a single human dominant allele disturbs kidney development by this route is not established.
The uterus is a Mullerian duct derivative, so failure of duct formation leaves it absent.
A hypomorphic allele may allow partial duct development, leaving a small uterus rather than none.
The upper vagina is a Mullerian duct derivative, so failure of duct formation can leave the vagina absent.
Without a functional uterus there is no menstruation, so failure of Mullerian duct formation presents as primary amenorrhea despite ovarian tissue.
Ovarian testosterone synthesis raises circulating testosterone.
Hirsutism is the androgen-dependent hair response to the raised circulating testosterone.
Acne is a cutaneous sign of the androgen excess.

Proposed link between disturbed WNT4-dependent kidney development and the renal agenesis of the index patient. Renal agenesis normally reflects failure of the ureteric bud rather than of nephron induction, and mouse Wnt4 loss leaves ureteric development intact, so the intermediate steps are unknown.

edges.description: Complete absence of the Mullerian duct in female null embryos.
edges.limitations: The mouse is homozygous null whereas patients are heterozygous for missense alleles, some dominant negative; heterozygous mice are not reported to share the phenotype, so the model shows the requirement for WNT4 rather than the human dosage sensitivity.

edges.description: Null ovaries express testosterone biosynthetic enzymes and secrete testosterone into the embryonic circulation.
edges.limitations: Androgen excess in the mouse is fetal and is read out as Wolffian duct maintenance; the human phenotype is adolescent clinical hyperandrogenism, which the perinatal-lethal knockout cannot show.

edges.description: Null metanephric mesenchyme fails to form pretubular aggregates.
edges.limitations: The null mouse has a severe bilateral nephrogenesis defect, while the human disease shows at most unilateral renal agenesis in a single case; the model establishes the renal role of WNT4 but not that heterozygous human alleles act through it.

edges.description: Partial Mullerian agenesis after combined mesenchymal loss of Wnt4 and Wnt5a.

nodes.description: In the ovary WNT4 represses the steroidogenic enzymes of the androgen pathway (CYP17A1, HSD3B2, and in the mouse also Cyp11a1 and Hsd17b enzymes) and, in the fetal mouse gonad, keeps adrenal-type steroidogenic precursor cells from migrating in. Loss of WNT4 releases this repression and the ovary synthesizes testosterone. In mice the excess androgen maintains the Wolffian ducts; in women it produces acne, hirsutism and raised serum testosterone.

nodes.description: The Mullerian (paramesonephric) duct is the anlage of the Fallopian tubes, uterus and upper vagina. WNT4 is needed for the migration of the cells that initiate the duct and for its posterior elongation; without it the duct fails to form, and its derivatives are absent or hypoplastic. In the reported patients the uterus was absent or hypoplastic while ovaries were present.

nodes.description: Heterozygous missense variants reduce WNT4 signalling. The four reported alleles (E226G, R83C, L12P, A233T) were each shown to be functionally defective, and R83C acts as a dominant negative, which would explain how a single allele produces a phenotype when heterozygous Wnt4 loss is silent in the mouse. The degree of loss differs between alleles: A233T only partly loses the ability to repress ovarian steroidogenic enzymes.

nodes.description: In the developing kidney Wnt4 acts as an autoinducer of the conversion of metanephric mesenchyme into the epithelial tubules that become nephrons. Wnt4-null mice fail at this step. In this disease only the index patient had a renal anomaly (unilateral renal agenesis), so the kidney arm is poorly characterized in humans and the mechanism is extrapolated from the mouse.

nodes.description: IVF with the patient's own oocytes and transfer to a gestational carrier is the established route to genetic parenthood in Mullerian agenesis, and uterus transplantation is an emerging alternative. In WNT4 deficiency the route depends on ovarian reserve, which may be reduced: follicle depletion was reported in one patient. No fertility outcomes specific to this disorder are published.

nodes.description: A hypomorphic Wnt4 allele allows some animals to survive to adulthood. The Mullerian duct forms in only about 45 percent of cases, and the resulting reproductive tract shows a poorly coiled oviduct, no endometrial glands and an undifferentiated myometrium. The model shows that reduced rather than absent WNT4 activity can still prevent or distort Mullerian development, which bears on the partial-loss human alleles.

nodes.description: Female Wnt4-null mice lack Mullerian ducts, retain Wolffian ducts and ectopically synthesize testosterone in the ovary, which is the combination seen in the human disease. Males are normal at birth. The knockout also fails to form nephrons and dies shortly after birth, so the adult reproductive phenotype cannot be studied in it.

evidence.reference_title: Female development in mammals is regulated by Wnt-4 signalling.
evidence.snippet: Wnt-4 is initially required in both sexes for formation of the Mullerian duct, then Wnt-4 in the developing ovary appears to suppress the development of Leydig cells; consequently, Wnt-4-mutant females ectopically activate testosterone biosynthesis.
